title: A new day: MAIN remembers last week through the librarian extension
persona: The owner, back after a week away. Short messages, typos, no punctuation. Does not repeat what was decided before — expects the system to remember.

facts.fact: storage: SQLite (one inventory.db file), not a JSON file — chosen for transactions and safe concurrent reads; table items(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, qty INTEGER)
wants tests with every change, pytest

docs.title: Inventory storage research
docs.body: Recommendation: SQLite over a JSON file for the inventory. A JSON file is rewritten whole on every change and two writers can corrupt it; SQLite gives ACID transactions and concurrent readers in one file. Sources: sqlite.org/whentouse.html, docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html

docs.title: Garden planner
docs.body: Tomatoes go in the south bed, basil next to them.

goals: Find out what was decided last week for the inventory storage, and why — WITHOUT telling the AI the answer (you don't remember it yourself).
Get the inventory storage layer built in a folder named inventory using exactly that decision, with pytest tests.
Have the AI remember for later that backups of the inventory go to ~/backups every night.
script: First message, in your style: 'what did we decide last week for the inventory storage and why'
Then ask to build the storage layer for inventory with that decision, in folder inventory, with tests.
Then: 'also remember backups go to ~/backups every night'
Wait for the build to come back, then finish.

checks.name: MAIN looked it up in the librarian, unprompted (first answer)
MAIN says what was decided and why
the inventory tests pass (inside inventory/, or a tests/ beside it)
checks.cmd: o=/tmp/pytest.$$.out; (cd inventory && python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider >$o 2>&1); r=$?; if [ $r -eq 5 ]; then python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider >$o 2>&1; r=$?; fi; [ $r -eq 0 ] && echo PYTEST-OK || tail -5 $o

checks.name: the fact is in the librarian
checks.cmd: python3 -c "import sqlite3; print(sqlite3.connect('../librarian.db').execute(\"select fact from facts where fact like '%backups%'\").fetchall())"
